model: GX device Modbus-TCP (Cerbo GX, Venus GX, Color Control GX)
equipment_type: Battery inverter (GX gateway for inverter/chargers, batteries and solar chargers)
applies_to: Victron GX devices running Venus OS with the Modbus-TCP service enabled; register list version 3.81 (document Rev 54). Core system, VE.Bus inverter/charger, battery, solar charger and ESS registers only.
summary: A Victron GX device is a Modbus-TCP gateway: one IP address on port 502, with the unit ID choosing which connected product you talk to (unit ID 100 for whole-system totals and ESS settings, other IDs for each Multi/Quattro, battery monitor or MPPT). Every register in this map is a single 16-bit integer whose raw value is divided by Victron's scale factor. The map covers system power flows and battery summary, VE.Bus AC/DC measurements, state, alarms and ESS mode 3 control, battery monitor/BMS values and alarms, solar charger readings, and the ESS mode 2 settings.

addressing.note: The 'Address' column of Victron's register list goes into the request as-is. Victron's GX Modbus-TCP manual reads VE.Bus input voltage (register 3) by setting the first request register to 3, so the listed number is the wire address. Clients that add or subtract one (Modicon 4xxxx entry) will be off by one register. Function codes 3 and 4 return identical data; all registers are listed here as holding registers, and writes use 6 or 16.

firmware: Venus OS; register list 3.81. Some registers need a minimum Venus version (e.g. 2716 needs 3.50+).

source.pages: Sheet 'Field list' (columns: dbus-service-name, Address, Type, Scalefactor, writable, dbus-unit); sheet 'Unit ID mapping'; sheet 'Document versions'

notes: Scale: Victron's 'Scalefactor' column is a divisor (engineering value = raw / scalefactor). It is converted here to a multiplier: scalefactor 10 -> scale 0.1, 100 -> 0.01, 0.1 -> 10, 0.01 -> 100, -10 -> -0.1 (consumed Ah is published as a positive raw number that means a negative Ah figure).

Left out on purpose: every 32-bit and 64-bit register (int32/uint32/uint64, e.g. system 868-918, VE.Bus energy counters 74-93 and ESS setpoints 96-101, battery 256 and 330, solar charger 792 and 3728, ESS 2716/2720/2722). Neither the register list nor Victron's GX Modbus-TCP manual or data communication whitepaper states the word order of multi-register values, so they are not listed. Each has a 16-bit equivalent listed here except the VE.Bus energy counters.

Left out: 2704 (ESS max inverter power). The register list gives scalefactor 0.1 (raw x 10 W) while Victron's ESS mode 2 and 3 guide describes the value as plain watts; the scale cannot be settled from the sources.

Left out: deprecated registers whose value is always 0 (267, 276-277, 297-300, 781), the deprecated ESS percentage switches 2701/2702, and the microgrid block 200-246 (213-222 are marked unsupported).
Not every product fills every register. A register that the selected device does not provide returns Modbus exception 02 (illegal data address); a block read that includes one fails as a whole.

ESS details (setpoint sign, 60-second rewrite rule in mode 3, inverted logic of 2708, 100 W units of 2706, -1 for no limit) come from Victron's 'ESS mode 2 and 3' guide, https://www.victronenergy.com/live/ess:ess_mode_2_and_3 (last modified 2024-10-14). Function codes, unit ID 0/100 and the error codes come from the 'GX Modbus-TCP Manual', https://www.victronenergy.com/live/ccgx:modbustcp_faq. Port 502 is stated in 'Data communication with Victron Energy products' (whitepaper on victronenergy.com).
Enum meanings are copied from the register list's dbus-unit column; VE.Bus error 32 and solar charger error 788 list only the codes the register list defines.

integration.summary: Enable the Modbus-TCP service on the GX, read the 'Available services' list to get each device's unit ID, then poll unit ID 100 (registers 817-866) for the system picture and the VE.Bus unit ID (registers 3-36) for the inverter/charger. All listed values are one 16-bit register each: apply the scale, and treat INT16 rows as signed.

minimum_registers.why: System battery state of charge (unit ID 100)
System battery power, + charging / - discharging (unit ID 100)
Switch position: remote on/off/charger-only (VE.Bus unit ID)
AC input current limit (VE.Bus unit ID)

integration.enable: Modbus-TCP is off by default. On the GX, enable it under Settings > Services > Modbus TCP (newer Venus OS: Settings > Integrations > Modbus TCP server). The same menu lists 'Available services' with each device's unit ID and shows the last Modbus error. ESS mode 3 control needs ESS mode set to external control (register 2902 = 3, or the GUI).
integration.watchdog: ESS mode 3: the VE.Bus power setpoints (37, 40, 41) must be rewritten at least every 60 seconds or the Multi drops to passthru. No general Modbus timeout is documented for other writes.
quirks: The unit ID picks the device, not the register: the same register number means different things on different unit IDs, and a register read on the wrong unit ID returns exception 02.
Unit ID 100 and unit ID 0 both reach the system service and the ESS settings; use 100 because many clients reject 0.

Since Venus OS 2.60 unit IDs are assigned dynamically and generally equal the device instance (up to 247). The 'Unit ID mapping' sheet keeps the old preferred IDs: 246 = CCGX VE.Bus port, 242 = Venus GX VE.Bus port, 227 = Cerbo GX VE.Bus port, 225 = CAN-bus BMS, 223/224/226 = Cerbo GX VE.Direct ports. Always confirm on the GX's Available services page.
Scale factors are divisors in Victron's sheet; several power registers have scalefactor 0.1 or 0.01, meaning the raw value must be MULTIPLIED (by 10 or 100).
Function 3 and 4 return the same data.
A block read must not include any register the device lacks (Victron's example: reading 1-100 on the VE.Bus unit fails because 1 and 2 do not exist).
setup: Give the GX a fixed IP (or DHCP reservation); Modbus-TCP listens on port 502.
No serial settings: RS485 is not used for this interface.
Unit IDs do not change after a reboot or power loss, per the GX Modbus-TCP manual.
gotchas: Parallel or three-phase VE.Bus systems cannot be addressed unit by unit; read the per-phase registers instead.
Inverter/charger configuration (absorption voltage etc.) cannot be changed over Modbus-TCP.
Exception 0A means the unit ID is known but no device answers on that port; 0B means the unit ID is not in the mapping list.
Battery history registers (284, 303 and similar) are not available from CAN-bus BMS batteries.

For ESS mode 2 grid setpoints on Venus 3.50 and later, Victron recommends the 32-bit register 2716 to avoid flash wear; it is not listed here because the word order is not documented, so 2700/2703 remain the documented 16-bit option.
